I’m using the repository’s `crimes` review workflow to validate the supplied scan against the actual client and API declarations, then I’ll separate true boundary disagreements from incidental findings and rank them by runtime impact.

The repository-local skill is stored above this runner directory, so I’m resolving that declared path before running the review checks.

The fixture confirms the reported declarations, but the global `crimes` binary is not on this runner’s `PATH`. I’m checking for the repository-built CLI locally; the supplied JSON remains the scan contract if no executable is present. One additional concern is already visible in source: some client URLs use the literal `:id`, which may be a separate production break beyond the scanner’s summarized route findings.

All four web-client operations are broken or unsafe against the current billing API. Ranking below reflects actual runtime behavior, not only the scanner’s severity labels.

| Rank | Contract disagreement | Production failure |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | `changeWorkspacePlan` sends `PUT /api/teams/:id/plan`; the API declares `POST /api/teams/{team_id}/plan`. The client also substitutes neither `id` nor `plan`. | Immediate **405**. Changing only the verb then produces **422** because `plan` is a required query parameter; fixing that still sends `team_id=":id"`. |
| 2 | `workspaceSeats(id)` sends the literal path `/api/teams/:id/seats`; the API expects a concrete identifier. | FastAPI can bind `":id"` as the identifier, producing a silent wrong-tenant lookup rather than an obvious error. The current handler ignores the ID, masking the defect. |
| 3 | `createWorkspace` calls `POST /api/workspaces`; the API exposes `POST /api/teams`. The API also requires a dictionary request body, while the client sends none. | Immediate **404**. Correcting only the path then produces **422** for the missing body. |
| 4 | `getWorkspace` calls `GET /api/workspaces/<id>`; the API exposes `GET /api/teams/{team_id}`. | Deterministic **404**, preventing workspace billing data from loading. This dynamic URL was not reported separately by the scanner. |
| 5 | The plan sets disagree: web has `free`, `pro`, `enterprise`; API has `free`, `pro`, `team`, `scale`. | `team`/`scale` can reach code typed as if they were impossible, causing missing UI branches. `enterprise` contradicts the API’s canonical enum. Because the change endpoint currently accepts `str` rather than `Plan`, it may silently accept an unsupported value instead of rejecting it. |
| 6 | The same tenant concept is named `workspace` in TypeScript and `team` in Python. | No direct runtime failure by itself, but it has already manifested as the `/workspaces` versus `/teams` route failures and makes future changes easy to apply on one side only. |

Evidence: [workspace-client.ts](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/d0b4a6f6-acd0-4986-8afe-011e15f736b2/scratchpad/evalwt/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:10), [routes.py](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/d0b4a6f6-acd0-4986-8afe-011e15f736b2/scratchpad/evalwt/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/api/billing/routes.py:10), and [plans.py](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/d0b4a6f6-acd0-4986-8afe-011e15f736b2/scratchpad/evalwt/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/api/billing/plans.py:10).

The scan’s `name_behavior_mismatch` finding for `getWorkspace` is not a client/API disagreement; an asynchronous HTTP GET is normal behavior for that name. I would record it as detector feedback:

```bash
crimes feedback 'name_behavior_mismatch::packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts::getWorkspace' \
  --verdict fp \
  --note "getWorkspace performs an ordinary HTTP GET and does not mutate billing state"
```

The durable fix is to make the FastAPI/OpenAPI definition canonical and generate the TypeScript routes and `Plan` type from it. The scan covered the three source files but excluded three JSON files and one TOML file.
